summary: Computes an oriented bounding box and a bounding sphere for mesh vertex data. Accumulates per-vertex statistics (sums of squares, cross-product terms, component sums) across all meshes, normalizes them into means and second moments, runs QRDecomposition to obtain the OBB eigenvector axes, builds a 4x4 D3D transform matrix from those axes, transforms each vertex through the D3D device, tracks the min/max bounds of the transformed corners, then finds the maximum squared distance of vertices from the stored center and writes its square root into this+0x18 as the bounding sphere radius. Returns the mesh count.

operations.description: Entry guard: mesh count at this+0x118 must be greater than 0 before the vertex-statistics accumulation pass runs.

Loop over each mesh element in the array at *(this+0x11C); each element is 64 bytes and carries the vertex count at +0x8, a vertex-data pointer at +0xC, and additional stride/layout fields at +0x10 and +0x14.
Per-mesh guard: the mesh's vertex count (*(this+0x11C) element +0x8) must be greater than 0 for its vertices to be processed.
Select vertex stride: bit 0x800000 of the flags at this+0x14 (tested via global 0x00800000) selects the 64-byte stride; otherwise a 48-byte stride is used.
Accumulate per-vertex statistics from the mesh vertex data: sums of squared X/Y/Z components, pairwise cross-product sums, and raw component sums.
Normalize the accumulated sums by the vertex count (1.0 divided by the count, sourced from global 0x0059E420) to form the mean and second-moment terms.
Assemble the symmetric 3x3 covariance matrix from the accumulated second-moment and cross-product terms.
Call QRDecomposition on the covariance matrix to obtain the oriented bounding box axes; the eigenvector basis is returned in a 3x3 result array.
Build a 4x4 D3D row-major transform matrix from the QR eigenvector basis, with zero and one entries supplied by the constants at globals 0x0059E420 and 0x0059E430.
Transform each vertex position through the D3D device matrix by dispatching through the device-wrapper pointer global dword_8B8F24 (vtable entry +4).
Track running min and max across the transformed corner coordinates to derive the axis-aligned bounding box extremes.
Final pass over all meshes computing the squared distance of each vertex from the stored center (this+0xDC, +0xE0, +0xE4) and keeping the maximum.
Store the square root of the maximum squared vertex distance into this+0x18 as the bounding sphere radius.
Return the mesh count (this+0x118) as the result.
